findings.claim: The discovery document advertises batchPath: "batch/calendar/v3", and no route serves it.
findings.evidence: POST http://localhost:45102/batch/calendar/v3 with a valid bearer token returns 404 {"message":"Not Found","documentation_url":"https://emulate.dev/google"} from core's catch-all (core/src/server.ts:94-102). It reproduces under an adapter mount: POST /emulate/google/batch/calendar/v3 -> 404. The string occurs exactly once in the repository, at calendar-discovery.ts:19, with no consumer and no route; git grep finds no /batch registration anywhere in packages. The new test file asserts batchPath zero times.
findings.layer: external HTTP boundary of the running emulator
findings.path: buildCalendarDiscoveryDocument -> served document -> client derives rootUrl + batchPath -> POST -> core catch-all 404
findings.impact: A discovery-driven client that batches (the documented reason batchPath exists) is told the endpoint is there. This is the precise thing the PR body says it avoids: 'without advertising unsupported Calendar operations'. The same PR deliberately omits showDeleted for that reason, so the omission standard is the author's own.

findings.claim: The empty root parameters block breaks the exact python client workflow the new docs teach.
findings.evidence: Upstream Calendar v3 carries alt, fields, key, oauth_token, prettyPrint, quotaUser, and userIp in the root parameters block; the emulated document ships {} (calendar-discovery.ts:20). google-api-python-client builds each method's accepted kwargs from the root parameters block plus STACK_QUERY_PARAMETERS only (discovery.py:130, 813, 837-845), and raises TypeError("Got an unexpected keyword argument") at discovery.py:1104-1106 before issuing any request. So service.events().list(calendarId='primary', fields='items(id)') raises client-side against the emulator and succeeds against Google. Aggravating: google.test.ts:993 asserts document.parameters toEqual({}), pinning the omission as correct.
findings.layer: google-api-python-client argmap construction, before any HTTP request
findings.path: root parameters {} -> _fix_up_parameters -> method argmap -> unknown kwarg -> TypeError
findings.impact: Every standard query parameter is unusable through the client the README, docs site, and SKILL.md all instruct the user to build. The failure is client-side, so no emulator log shows it.
findings.verification_gap: python3 was unavailable in this environment, so the TypeError is confirmed from library source rather than from an executed call. The document-level differential against the live upstream document is executed and confirmed.

findings.claim: singleEvents and the orderBy enum are advertised but never read, and the emulator accepts values the document excludes.
findings.evidence: singleEvents=true and singleEvents=false returned byte-identical bodies on a live listener. orderBy=updated returned 200 although the advertised enum is ["startTime"]. orderBy=startTime without singleEvents=true returned 200 where upstream returns 400. The emulator has no recurrence model at all: no hits for recurrence, recurringEventId, RRULE, or originalStartTime anywhere in the google package.
findings.layer: external HTTP boundary of the running emulator
findings.path: advertised parameter -> route handler ignores it -> unchanged response
findings.impact: Low. Advertising an inert parameter is a weaker version of F1: the document overstates fidelity, but a client passing it gets a plausible answer rather than a 404. Worth a decision, not necessarily a change.

findings.claim: The new suite cannot fail for the reasons this document can be wrong.
findings.evidence: Expected values are the same literals the builder hardcodes, so no assertion has an oracle independent of the implementation. batchPath, the one field introduced at the root of the document, is asserted zero times. No assertion connects a document-advertised path to a reachable route. Line 993 pins parameters == {} as correct, so a fix for F2 would turn the suite red. The genuine exception is line 1140, a closed-graph check over $refs.
findings.path: document literal -> test expectation copied from the same literal
findings.impact: The 18 green tests certify that the builder returns what the builder returns. They are a change detector, not a correctness oracle, which is why both actionable findings required an external document to surface.
